## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** no functional defect found in the reviewed scope; two minor points follow below. Every new lock request passes through `beginLock()`, so moving the reset there covers the lock paths that previously skipped `omarchy-system-lock`. Securing the lock never waits on the new processes.

| Lock path | Route to the lock service | Reset at base | Reset at this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Manual, idle, lid close | `omarchy-system-lock` -> `omarchy-shell lock lock` -> `beginLock()` | wrapper | `beginLock()`, wrapper, after secure |
| Suspend (`systemctl suspend`) | `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` -> IPC `lock()` -> `beginLock()` | none | `beginLock()`, after secure |
| Shell restart relock | `omarchy-restart-shell` -> IPC `lock()` -> `beginLock()` | none | `beginLock()`, after secure |
| Stranded-lock recovery | `recoverStrandedLock()` -> `beginLock()` | none | `beginLock()`, after secure |

**Verified:** Quickshell 0.3.1 `Process` starts `hyprctl` through `QProcess::start()` without waiting for it, and the lock sequence (stabilize timer, compositor `locked` event, `secure`) never waits on either reset. A missing or failing `hyprctl` cannot stop or delay the lock. On Hyprland 0.56.2, `switchxkblayout all 0` visits every keyboard in the input manager, physical and virtual, and index 0 is always in range. Hyprland's session-lock code changes focus only, not layout. The reset remains best-effort: there is no exit check or readback of `active_layout_index`.

### Comment on the second reset describes a race the source does not show

`// Reapply after the lock is secure in case the first IPC call raced it.`

Nothing in lock setup undoes a completed reset. The first reset is started at least 500 ms (the stabilize timer) before the session lock is requested, and neither Hyprland's lock creation nor the lock surface's focus changes the keyboard group. The second call is still useful as a best-effort retry: the first asynchronous call may have failed, or the layout may have changed in between (a layout shortcut, a newly connected keyboard, a virtual-keyboard client).

**Impact:** readers may assume the lock itself can restore the previous layout, which the source does not support.

**Suggested change:** reword the comment to state what the call covers, for example `// Retry after the lock is secure: the earlier async reset may have failed, or the layout may have changed since.`

### Resets are not cancelled on unlock

`finishUnlock()` and the branch that handles the compositor dropping the lock leave `layoutResetBeforeLock` and `layoutResetAfterLock` alone. In Quickshell 0.3.1, setting `running = true` while a run is still in progress also queues one rerun after it exits. A reset can therefore take effect after unlock and override a layout the user switched to deliberately. This requires the `hyprctl` process to take longer to reach Hyprland than the unlock plus that switch; a normally scheduled `hyprctl` connects within milliseconds.

**Impact:** under that narrow condition, one unwanted switch to index 0 after unlock. No security impact.

**Suggested change:** setting `layoutResetBeforeLock.running = false` and `layoutResetAfterLock.running = false` in both unlock paths drops any queued rerun and stops a process that has not yet reached Hyprland.

**Note:** suspending while the session is already locked still does not reset the layout, because IPC `lock()` skips `beginLock()` when the session is locked. This matters only if the layout is switched on the lock screen before suspend, and it is outside the PR's stated scope of new lock requests.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the lock paths in Omarchy at the PR head, Quickshell 0.3.1 `Process` and session lock, Hyprland 0.56.2 `switchxkblayout`, session lock and IPC handling, and Qt 6.11.2 `QProcess` start. Deployed Quickshell and Qt versions may differ from those inspected. `Service.qml` parsed with `qmlformat` at base and head in an isolated sandbox. No lock, suspend, compositor or hardware testing; the end-to-end layout on the password field and all timing statements are source-derived, not measured.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up questions, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
